Prosecution case, in brief, is that one Ghanashyam Das, had lodged an FIR on 20- 11-2009 before the Lahdoigarh Police Outpost, inter-alia, alleging therein that during the night of 17-11-2009 at around 12 midnight, the petitioner, herein, had entered into the bedroom of his daughter by cutting the rope of the door and committed rape on her.
It was further projected that the family members of the informant were awakened on hearing the sound which had emanated during the commission of rape by the petitioner, herein, upon his daughter.

The members of the family on moving to the room of the informant's daughter, they found the presence of the petitioner, therein, and as he was tried to be apprehended, the petitioner, herein, fled from the place leaving behind his mobile phone, money bag and tobacco pot.
On receipt of the said FIR Lahdoigarh Police Outpost recorded G.D. Entry No. 384 dated 20-11-2009 and forwarded the same to Teok Police Station.

Accordingly, Teok P.S. Case No.
108/2009 came to be registered.
Page No.# 3/11
On completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer (I/O) had laid charge- sheet against the present petitioner under Section 457/ 376 IPC.
The case being committed to the court of Sessions, the same was transferred to the court of Assistant Sessions Judge, Jorhat for disposal.

sentences.text:
The learned Trial Court upon appreciating the evidences coming on record framed charge under Section 457/ 376 IPC against the petitioner,
herein.
The charges on being read over and explained to the petitioner, he having pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried, a trial ensued.
During the trial, the prosecution had examined 09 (nine) witnesses and thereafter, the petitioner was examined under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

On conclusion of the trial, the learned Trial Court on examination of the evidences coming on record, proceeded vide judgment dated 27-01-2012 to convict the petitioner, herein, under Section 457/ 376 IPC and sentenced him as noticed,
hereinabove.

The petitioner being aggrieved by his conviction by the learned Trial Court vide judgment dated 27-01-2012, assailed the same before the court of learned Sessions Judge, Jorhat by filing an appeal being Crl. Appeal No. 08/2012.

The learned Appellate Court, upon appreciating the evidences coming on record, proceeded vide judgment dated 28-04-2012 to dismiss the appeal and thereby upholding the conviction and sentence of the petitioner, herein, by the learned Trial Court under Section 457/ 376 IPC.
Being aggrieved, the petitioner has instituted the present revision petition.

sentences.text: I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and also perused the materials Page No.# 4/11 available on record.

5. The learned Trial Court upon examining the evidences coming on record vide judgment dated 27-01-2012 had drawn the following points for determination:-
"i) Whether the accused committed lurking house trespass by night by entering into the house belonging to the informant Ghanashyam Das after cutting the rope of the door within the period after the sunset and before sun rise ?
ii) Whether the accused committed rape on Numoli Das, her daughter of the informant against her will & consent?"
6. Thereafter, the learned Trial Court upon appreciating the evidences coming on record with regard to the point No. 1 had drawn the following conclusions:
"10. Now, coming to the point No.1 whether the accused person committed house breaking by night, let me to appreciate the evidence of the witnesses on record hereunder.

To constitute a lurking house trespass or house breaking by night in order to commit an offence punishable with imprisonment, requires following ingredients,
that the accused committed house trespass by night or house breaking by night, that the accused did so after having made preparation for committing an offence punishable with imprisonment.
In the case in my hand, the victim in her deposition clearly stated that she maintained love affairs with the accused since last two years before the incident took place.

Under the guise of maintaining love affairs with her,
the accused used to take her in the tea garden and had sex with her.
But, she never disclosed such incident to anybody as the accused promised her to get marry.
She also stated that on the very fateful night of 16.11.2009 at 12 p.m, the accused entered into her sleeping room by cutting the rope of the door and raped her.

In course of doing such act by the accused, somehow, her leg touched the body of her sister who,
was sharing her bed.
On being touched the body of her sister, the latter raised shouting.
Hearing the shouting of her sister, her father came to her room with a CHAAKI in his hand and found the presence of the accused in her room.

Seeing the presence of her father, the accused flee away leaving his Money Bag, Mobile Set and one Tobacco pot on the spot which were subsequently seized by the police after preparation of seizure list.

She was extensively cross-examined by the defence, but her evidence remained unassailed on the point of accused entered into her bedroom by cutting the rope of the door on the very fateful night and committed rape on her.

Rather her evidence found corroboration from the evidence of P.w.1, the father of the Page No.# 5/11 victim, P.W.5 Smti Ruma Das, the wife of the victim's brother, P.W.6- Dilip Das- brother of the victim.

sentences.text: P.W.1 informant Ghanashyam Das deposed that on the very night of the incident at 12 p.m, receiving the sound from the bedroom of the victim, he woke up and went to the bedroom of the victim where he found the presence of the accused.
Finding the accused present in the room, he tried to hold the accused, but the accused managed to flee away.
He stated that the accused left his Mobile Set, Money bag and one tobacco pot on the spot at the time of flee away.

On being asked, the victim reported that she maintained love affairs with the accused since last two years and she could not disclose such relation of the accused to anybody due to accused threatened her with dire consequence.
It was also reported by her that the accused under the inducement of marry her, maintained illicit relation with her.
The victim also reported that on the very fateful night, the accused committed rape on her.

P.w.5 Ruma Das stated that on the very fateful night of occurrence, hearing the noise of shouting took place in the bedroom of the victim, she rashed to the bedroom of the victim and came to know from the victim that the accused person entered into her bed room by cutting the rope of the door and had committed rape on her.

She also disclosed that the accused, at the time of flee away from the bedroom of the victim,
left his Mobile handset, Money Bag and one Tobacco pot there.

P.W.6 Dilip Das deposed that hearing the noise of shouting took place in the bed room of the victim on the very fateful night, while he came out from his own room,
his father told him that the accused person flee away from the bedroom of the victim as soon as he lighted the lamp.
He stated that on arrival at the bed room, he found the dress of the victim in not proper way.
On being asked, the victim reported the fact of accused entered into her bedroom by cutting the rope of the door and committed rape on her.
He also found the Mobile set, Money Bag and one tobacco pot were lying on the bed of the victim which were left by the accused at the time of flee away.

11. All the above noted witnesses were duly cross examined by the defence, but the defence failed to elicit anything to disbelieve their evidence to the extent of accused entered into the bedroom of the victim on the very fateful night by cutting the rope of the door.

Rather the evidence of above-noted witnesses are found consistent to each other in respect of accused found present in the bedroom of the victim and on arrival of the witnesses on the spot, he flee away by leaving his Mobile set, Money Bag and one tobacco pot there.
It is also apparent from the evidence of the witnesses that the accused entered into the bedroom of the victim in order to commit rape on the victim.

The Ld. Counsel for the accused submitted that the victim being the major girl maintained affairs with the accused since last two years without disclosing the same to any other person presumably shows that the victim was one of the Page No.# 6/11 consenting parties to the incident took place.
So, the accused cannot be held liable for house-breaking.

But, I am unable to accept the submission of the Ld. Counsel on the ground that the accused person entered into the bedroom of the victim without Rana Das vs State Of Assam on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28458986/
4 obtaining the consent of the victim on the very fateful night.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the accused, in his examination U/S.313 of Cr.P.C tried to say that his Money Bag, Mobile set and tobacco pot was missing on the road.
The accused, in support of finding his Money Bag, Mobile set and tobacco pot on the road, did not adduce any evidence.

Rather the evidence of victim P.w.2, her father- P.w.1, her brother's wife Ruma Das-P.w.5 and her brother- P.W.6 who, immediately after the occurrence took place arrived at the site of the occurrence categorically stated that the Money Beg, Mobile set and Tobacco pot belonging to the accused found in the bedroom of the victim which were subsequently seized by the I/O after preparation of seizure list marked Ext.2. P.W.8 1/0 in his evidence stated that on 20.11.09 while he made visit to the place of occurrence, the victim girl handed over one Nokia Mobile hand set with SIM card, one Money Bag containing currency Notes of Rs.30/-, one pocket diary and along with the same one tobacco pot alleged to have left by the accused on the very fateful night of occurrence and he seized the same after preparation of seizure list in presence of the witnesses marked Ext.2.

P.W.2, P.w., 1, P.W.5, P.w.6 and P.w.8 identified the seized articles marked as M.Ext.1.
12.
Thus, from the above discussion, it is crystal clear that the accused person entered into the bedroom of the victim by cutting the rope of the door in order to commit rape on the victim.
So, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has successfully proved the charge U/S.457 of I.P.C beyond all shadow of doubt, hence, the accused person is liable to be convicted for the same."

7. Having drawn the said conclusions, the learned Trial Court proceeded to examine the point as whether the petitioner, herein, had committed rape upon the daughter of the informant against her will and consent and drew the following conclusions:-
"13. Turning to the point whether the accused committed rape on the victim against her will and without her consent.

The victim, in her evidence, as well as in her statement recorded U/S.164 of Cr.P.C stated in clear terms that she maintained love affairs with the accused since last two years before the alleged incident took place.

She also stated that prior to the incident took place, the accused used to maintained sexual relation with her by taking her to the garden on few occasion and she did not disclose the same to anybody as the accused promised her to get marry.

It is stated by the victim that on the very fateful night while she was sleeping with her sister in her bedroom, the accused entered into her bedroom by cutting the rope of the door and committed rape on her.

In course of committing rape on her by the accused, suddenly her leg touched the body of her sister who Page No.# 7/11 was sharing her bed, the latter raised shouting and on hearing the shouting of her sister, her father came to her bedroom and found the accused present there.

Her evidence to the effect of accused committed rape on her after entering into her bedroom by cutting the rope of the door have been fully corroborated by P.W.1- father of the victim, P.W.5- wife of the brother of the victim and P.W.6- brother of the victim.

sentences.text: The victim also told them that the accused maintained sexual relation with the victim for last two years under the promise to marry her, even the accused prohibited her from divulging the relation maintained by him with the victim with the threat of dire consequence.
So, she could not divulge the relation to anybody.

P.W.3 Pronita Bora stated that one day, the accused person came to her house and altercated with Ghanashyam Das, the informant, i.e., the father of the victim, on the matter of maintaining illicit relation with the victim girl and in course of such altercation, the accused expressed his readiness to get marry the victim.
The defence did not dispute the said evidence at the time of cross-examination.

P.w.4 Dipali Bora stated that on the next day of the incident took place, he was reported to the effect of accused committed rape on the victim in the night of 17.11.2009 by entering into her bedroom after cutting the rope of the door.
He stated that on 19.11.2009, a meeting of Mohila Samittee was held to resolve the matter of accused committed rape on the victim where he was one of the attendants.
He stated that in the meeting, the victim reported that the accused person maintained sexual relation with her under the promise to marry her.
P.w.7 made similar statement to the P.w.4 regarding holding of Mohila Samittee meeting to resolve the matter of sexual harassment to the victim by the accused.
But, the meeting ended without any result due to absence of the accused.
The evidence of P.W.8 I/0 found formal in nature to the extent of carry out investigation of the case.

The only disclosure part of his cross-examination is that the victim did not disclose before him about the accused committed rape on her by dragging her inside the tea garden and she also did not state before him to the effect of her leg touched with the body of her sister at the time of accused committing rape on her on the very fateful night and as a result, her sister raised shouting.
He also confirmed that P.w.1 Ghanashyam Das did not disclose before him that on hearing the sound, he came to the bedroom of the victim.

Though the witnesses were duly cross-examined by the defence, but the defence failed to rebut their testimonies on the material point of accused committed rape on the victim on the very fateful night.

P.W.9 Dr. Anador Neog, in his deposition,
supporting the medical examination report of the victim Numoli Das stated that on 20.11.2009, he examined the victim and found no injury on her body and her age is above 18 years and she is carrying pregnancy for twelve Page No.# 8/11 week's.
The Ld. counsel for the accused submitted that though the doctor found the victim carrying pregnancy more than 12 weeks, but the doctor did not give any opinion regarding recent sexual intercourse.
Moreover, the victim found to be consenting party to have sex with the accused.
So, the evidence of the victim cannot be relied that the accused committed sexual intercourse on the very fateful night against her will.

But, I am unable to accept the submission of the Ld. counsel on the ground that the accused entered into the bedroom of the victim on the very fateful night by cutting Rana Das vs State Of Assam on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28458986/
6 the rope of the door and committed sexual intercourse with her.

sentences.text: The act of the accused found to be against the will of the victim.

The fact of accused person entered into the bedroom of the victim on the very fateful night coupled with the disclosure of the victim that the accused committed rape on her on the very fateful night unerringly pointed towards the inference of the accused committed rape on the victim on the very fateful night.
14. In view of the above, I am of the opinion that the prosecution has successfully proved the ingredience of charge U/S.376 of I.P.C against the accused beyond all shadow of doubt.
Therefore, the accused is liable to be convicted for the offence punishable U/S.376 of I.P.C."
8. Basing on the said conclusions, the petitioner, herein, was convicted under Section 457/ 376 IPC and sentenced as noticed hereinabove.
This Court has considered the conclusions drawn by the learned Trial Court and also the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the parties in the present proceeding.

On consideration of the conclusions drawn by the learned Trial Court, this Court finds that the conviction of the petitioner, herein, was based primarily on the evidence of the victim who had deposed during the trial as PW-2.

The victim girl (PW-2) during her deposition had deposed that she was in a love affair with the petitioner, herein, for 02 years prior to the incident and she was taken by the petitioner, under the said pretext, to the garden and was raped.
She further deposed that the members of the family was not aware of this thing and she had engaged with physical relationship with the accused, herein, as he had promised to marry her.
The PW-2 also deposed that on 16-11-2009 at around 12 midnight, the petitioner had entered their house by cutting the bamboo door and then committed rape on her.
She Page No.# 9/11 further deposed that while committing rape on her, her younger sister woke up and screamed as her (victim girl's) leg brushed against her body.

She further deposed that hearing the commotion, her father who was sleeping in the adjacent room had come to her room with a lamp and her father seen the petitioner, herein, who thereafter fled there-from.
She further deposed that the petitioner, herein, while fleeing from the place had dropped his wallet, mobile phone and a tobacco container.
She deposed that her father later approached the Mahila Samity informing about the said incident.
However, the Mahila Samity could not trace out the petitioner, herein, and accordingly, her father lodged an ejahar before the police.

9. During her cross, she had not stated either to the police or before the Hon'ble Court while making her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that at the time of the incident when her leg had brushed her sister, her sister had woken up and had screamed leading to her father coming to her room.

10. A perusal of the evidences adduced by the PW-2 would go to reveal that while it is deposed that the petitioner, herein, had committed rape on her on the faithful night, it was not deposed that she had in any manner resisted the same and raised any hue and cry while she was being subjected to rape.
The evidence of the PW-2 also does not bring to the forefront that the petitioner, herein, had cupped her mouth dis-enabling her from shouting.

The evidence reveals that on the same bed at the relevant point of time, when she was subjected to sexual assault, her sister was also sleeping and it was only when the victim's leg had brushed against the body of her sister, the sister woke up and Rana Das vs State Of Assam on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28458986/
7 screamed leading her father coming to her room.

sentences.text:
The said evidence adduced by PW-2 raises an Page No.# 10/11 issue as to whether the sexual intercourse as committed in the matter by the petitioner,
herein, upon the victim girl was with the consent of the victim girl, inasmuch as she is not found to have resisted to such act on the part of the petitioner, herein.
The said aspect of the matter was not considered in its proper perspective by the learned Trial Court.

The evidences of the PW-2 having projected a situation wherein the sexual intercourse as committed upon her by the petitioner,
herein, can also be held to be one done with the consent of the victim girl, a doubt arises with regard to the projection made in the matter by the victim girl (PW-2) and accordingly, the said doubt being a probable one the benefit there-under has to be extended to the petitioner, herein.

Considering the evidence adduced by the PW-2, i.e. the victim girl, this Court is of the considered view that the petitioner and the victim girl being in a relationship for more than 02 years prior to the said incident, the allegation that the petitioner had entered into their house by cutting the rope of the door and had committed rape upon the victim girl on the faithful night does not inspire confidence of this Court and accordingly, this Court is of the considered view that basing on the said evidence it was not permissible to convict the petitioner, herein, under Section 457/ 376 IPC.
11.
In view of the discussions, this Court is of the considered view that the conviction of the petitioner, herein, under Section 457/ 376 IPC would mandate interference.

The learned Appellate Court while considering the appeal preferred in the matter by the petitioner, herein, had also not examined the evidence adduced by the PW-2 in its proper perspective and accordingly, the conclusions drawn by the learned Appellate Court would also not mandate any acceptance.

Accordingly, the conviction of the petitioner, herein, Page No.# 11/11 under Section 457/ 376 IPC along with the judgment dated 27-01-2012 passed by the learned Assistant Sessions Judge, Jorhat in Sessions Case No. 24(JJ)/2010 and the judgment dated 28-04-2012 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Jorhat in Crl. Appeal No. 08/2012, stand set aside.
12. The petitioner is set at liberty and the bail bond executed stand discharged.
13. With the above observations and directions, the present revision petition stands allowed.
14. Registry to send back the TCR forthwith along with a copy of the present order for information and necessary action.
